title: Erdős Problem #140: Density of 3-AP-Free Sets
description: Let r₃(N) be the size of the largest subset of {1,...,N} with no 3-term arithmetic progression. Prove r₃(N) ≪ N/(log N)^C for every C > 0. SOLVED by Kelley-Meka (2023).

overview.historicalContext: Roth (1953) proved r₃(N) = o(N), showing 3-AP-free sets have density 0. Decades of improvements followed: Bourgain (2008), Sanders (2011), Bloom-Sisask (2020). Kelley-Meka (2023) finally proved Erdős's conjecture that r₃(N) = O(N/(log N)^C) for all C > 0, resolving the $500 prize.
overview.problemStatement: Define r₃(N) = max{ |A| : A ⊆ {1,...,N}, A contains no non-trivial 3-term arithmetic progression }. Erdős conjectured that r₃(N) ≪ N/(log N)^C for every C > 0. Kelley and Meka (2023) proved this is true.
overview.proofStrategy: The formalization defines 3-APs, the Roth number r₃(N), and proves it's achieved by some set. Historical bounds by Roth, Bourgain, Sanders, and Bloom-Sisask are recorded as axioms. The Kelley-Meka theorem is the main axiom resolving the problem. Corollaries about density decay and the k-term generalization are included.
keyInsights: r₃(N) is well-defined and achieved (verified theorem)
Historical progression: o(N) → O(N/√log log N) → O(N log log N⁵/log N) → O(N/(log N)^{1+c})
Kelley-Meka (2023): r₃(N) = O(N/(log N)^C) for ALL C > 0
Behrend lower bound: r₃(N) ≥ N/exp(c√log N) - gap remains open

sections.title: Problem Statement and Background
sections.summary: States Erdős Problem #140: prove $r_3(N) \ll N/(\log N)^C$ for every $C > 0$. Outlines the 70-year history from Roth (1953) through Kelley-Meka (2023).

sections.title: 3-Term Arithmetic Progressions
sections.summary: Defines IsAP3 (the condition $2b = a + c$ with $a < b < c$), Is3APFree for sets of reals, and Finset3APFree for finite sets. These are the basic predicates for the entire formalization.

sections.title: The Roth Number r₃(N)
sections.summary: Defines $r_3(N)$ as the maximum cardinality of a 3-AP-free subset of $\{0, \ldots, N\}$. Proves r3_achieved: the supremum is attained (nonempty bounded set of naturals).

sections.title: Historical Upper Bounds
sections.summary: Axiomatizes the four milestone upper bounds: Roth ($o(N)$, 1953), Bourgain ($O(N/\sqrt{\log\log N})$, 2008), Sanders ($O(N(\log\log N)^5/\log N)$, 2011), and Bloom-Sisask ($O(N/(\log N)^{1+c})$, 2020).

sections.title: The Kelley-Meka Theorem (2023)
sections.summary: Axiomatizes the main result: for all $C > 0$ there exists $K > 0$ such that $r_3(N) \leq KN/(\log N)^C$ for $N \geq 3$. Proves erdos_140_solved as a direct application.

sections.title: Consequences and Corollaries
sections.summary: Derives r3_superlogarithmic (density decays faster than any inverse log power) and r3_density_vanishes ($r_3(N)(\log N)^C/N \to 0$) from the Kelley-Meka theorem.

sections.title: Behrend Lower Bound
sections.summary: Axiomatizes Behrend's 1946 lower bound $r_3(N) \geq N \cdot \exp(-c\sqrt{\log N})$. The gap between this and Kelley-Meka's upper bound remains a major open problem.

sections.title: Verified 3-AP-Free Examples
sections.summary: Machine-verifies that $\{0\}$ and $\{1,2,4,5,10,11,13,14\}$ are 3-AP-free using omega tactic and case analysis. The latter set is the first 8 elements of the greedy sequence (OEIS A003278).

sections.title: The Greedy 3-AP-Free Sequence
sections.summary: Defines the greedy construction that adds the smallest integer avoiding 3-APs. Axiomatizes that the greedy sequence is 3-AP-free. Growth rate is approximately $n^{\log 2/\log 3}$.

sections.title: k-Term AP Generalization
sections.summary: Generalizes to $k$-term APs: defines IsAPk, FinsetkAPFree, $r_k(N)$, and states the conjecture that $r_k(N) = O(N/(\log N)^C)$ for all $k \geq 3$. Proves the $k = 3$ case from Kelley-Meka. The $k \geq 4$ cases remain open.

sections.title: Summary and Problem Status
sections.summary: Summarizes the formalization: 4 verified theorems, 9 axioms encoding historical results, and the Kelley-Meka resolution. Lists open questions including the Behrend gap and $k \geq 4$ generalization.

crossReferences.description: Erdős #16 concerns Szemerédi regularity and density of arithmetic progressions — the same circle of problems that includes 3-AP density bounds

conclusion.summary: Erdős Problem #140 is SOLVED (Kelley-Meka 2023). The maximum size of a 3-AP-free subset of {1,...,N} satisfies r₃(N) = O(N/(log N)^C) for all C > 0. This 70-year problem from Roth's 1953 breakthrough was resolved with a novel spectral approach.
conclusion.implications: The Kelley-Meka theorem is a major breakthrough in additive combinatorics. It essentially determines the order of r₃(N) up to the gap with Behrend's lower bound. The techniques may apply to other Ramsey-type problems.
openQuestions: What is the true order of r₃(N)? (Behrend gap)
Does r_k(N) = O(N/(log N)^C) hold for k ≥ 4?
Is r₃(N) = Θ(N/exp(c√log N)) matching Behrend?
Can Kelley-Meka techniques improve k ≥ 4 bounds?
